set.bio.backstory: Raised on the rooftops of the Tangle, Kit could climb before they could read and pick a lock before they could sign their name. lore: Admits an 'arrangement' with the Curator for six years: she left his Market alone, and he fed her the names of rival relic smugglers. Swears it never touched the Magpie: 'I begged her not to go that night.' (Kit believed him.)
Says his buyer for the Eye is 'a foreign collector who pays in gold and asks no questions.' He won't name them.
Wants the Eye because it's 'the one thing in that building she can't replace'. Revenge, he says.

CONFESSED (to Kit, Day 1, 10:50): he sold the Magpie to the Curator six years ago. He gave Lucienne Varne the night and the skylight in exchange for six years of peace for his Market. She promised him a trial and put Marisol on display in the Hall of Infamy instead.

His buyer for the Eye is 'the Emissary', a masked foreigner offering 60,000 crowns. Crane means to leave Vessarine for good once it's sold. He hired Kit 'because you'd do it for her, and I needed someone who would.'

inventory.source: stolen: pried off Sergeant Varga's chained hand in the Heron's brig

inventory.description: An iron stage-door key on a red ribbon. The Carrow Theatre, a burned-out opera house in the Tangle, owned through a dead man's name by Crane. The crew's safehouse.
inventory.name: Key to the Carrow Theatre
inventory.source: gift: Valentin Crane, on accepting the job

inventory.description: Six lead pistol balls and a powder flask from Brask's pouch
inventory.name: Firearm Bullets (6)

inventory.description: A heavy signet of gold-inlaid silver: the Meridian sun-and-key over a pair of crossed keys, the mark of an Acquisitions Office lieutenant. Hedda will know what it opens. It stays good only until the Meridian learns Brask is dead.
inventory.name: Collector-Lieutenant's Sigil

inventory.description: Signed 'A. Thorne, Captain of Wardens'. Wanted for questioning over the Night Market: Hedda Vask (dwarf, formerly of the Wardens); a halfling scholar, likely T. Fenwick; a red-haired woman, a singer; a young man, dark-haired, a thief. No names for the last two.
inventory.name: Warrant for Questioning

inventory.description: Found sewn into the lining of Brask's coat. In a precise, elegant hand: 'B. The Heron's arrangement is ended. Bring me the Magpie's key. Whole. L.V.'
inventory.name: Sealed Note (L.V.)
inventory.source: loot: sewn into the lining of Brask's coat

inventory.description: The title to Crane's gambling barge, signed over as collateral: 'held in trust by K. Corvell until the Emissary's price is paid'. Worthless to sell in secret, but priceless as leverage.
inventory.name: Deed to the Gilded Heron
inventory.source: reward: signed over by Valentin Crane

inventory.description: In Crane's copperplate hand and sealed with his heron signet: 'I, V. Crane, owe the bearer and crew one half of whatever price the Ysmeran Eye fetches from the buyer called the Emissary: thirty thousand crowns at the agreed sixty thousand. Payable on sale, before anything else.'
inventory.name: Crane's Promissory Note
inventory.source: reward: written by Valentin Crane under duress

inventory.name: Rapier
inventory.note: Valentin Crane's walking cane: black lacquered wood with a silver heron's-head handle. A twist of the handle draws a slim, needle-pointed blade. It passes for a gentleman's cane anywhere a sword would draw looks. The engine treats it as a Rapier.
inventory.source: loot: the blade hidden inside Crane's heron's-head cane (a sword-cane)

Recognised Kit as the Magpie's son on sight. He knew her, and speaks of her 'end' as if he saw it.
Cracked under good cop / bad cop. Says: the Magpie isn't dead; she's the statue called 'The Thief' in the Hall of Infamy. 'Nobody dies in that building. The Curator doesn't waste pieces.'

lore: Collector-Sergeant Dunstan Varga: the Meridian Acquisitions Office's leg-breaker. Testified against Hedda at her trial six years ago. Unconscious and captured.
Recognised Kit as the Magpie's son on sight. He knew her, and speaks of her 'end' as if he saw it.
Cracked under good cop / bad cop. Says: the Magpie isn't dead; she's the statue called 'The Thief' in the Hall of Infamy. 'Nobody dies in that building. The Curator doesn't waste pieces.'
Says Crane sold the Magpie out six years ago: 'The Heron sang. Six years of peace for his Market.'
Says Captain Aldric Thorne killed Lt. Emeric Dane with Hedda's axe while she was knocked out, because Dane saw 'the green light' and wouldn't stay quiet.
Says the Curator is 'cleaning house' before the Gala, and every Warden is ordered to wear smoked-glass visors at midnight. He doesn't know why.
Wears a Warden's sigil ring (sun and key). He claims it will lead the Meridian to him.
Kit took his Warden's sigil ring.
Refused to write a confession for Hedda (her Intimidation: natural 1). The same approach can't be tried again for 24 hours.

Turned down Sera's deal (Persuasion 13 vs DC 15) because he doesn't trust a crew that kills witnesses. His terms: the hood comes off, and he's out of Vessarine BEFORE he testifies. His attitude has softened to Indifferent after being fed and treated. Sera can't make that same pitch again for 24 hours.
Sera, in private: 'Your fate is tied to ours.' If he doesn't agree next time, he goes into the mill race. He has the night to think it over (Day 1, 19:45).

inventory.description: Six close-written pages torn from the back of a spellbook, in a small, furious hand with diagrams. THE BLINK: at the Grand Conjunction the Orrery's last ring locks at the stroke of midnight, and the whole ward lattice goes dead for about three minutes and ten seconds. Every sigil plate, every alarm chime, and the Curator's own plate at the Undercroft door all go dark. The Brass Wardens are bound to the lattice and SHOULD stand still for the Blink ('should' underlined twice). THE HEART: a brass focal chamber in the Orrery works, directly under the great lens. Reach it by the Staff Only stair from the Rotunda, or from the Undercroft side. One door, as of eight years ago. The Eye sits in a cradle; the Orrery opens a clockwork iris over it at midnight on its own ('the lids'). THE EYE: while the lids are open it can be struck: bludgeoning or piercing only, and it's small, hard and glassy, perhaps as hard to hit as a knight in plate. Anyone in the Heart without a smoked-glass visor when the iris opens will begin to turn to stone. A Warden's gala visor will do. At the foot, underlined: 'This is how it was EIGHT YEARS AGO. She has had eight years to change it. Look before you leap. T.F.'
inventory.name: Tobias's Notes on the Blink and the Heart
inventory.source: gift: written by Tobias Fenwick in exchange for the Codex

inventory.description: Six close-written pages torn from the back of a spellbook, in a small, furious hand with diagrams. THE BLINK: at the Grand Conjunction the Orrery's last ring locks at the stroke of midnight, and the whole ward lattice goes dead for about three minutes and ten seconds. Every sigil plate, every alarm chime, and the Curator's own plate at the Undercroft door all go dark. The Brass Wardens are bound to the lattice and SHOULD stand still for the Blink ('should' underlined twice). THE HEART: a brass focal chamber in the Orrery works, directly under the great lens. Reach it by the Staff Only stair from the Rotunda, or from the Undercroft side. One door, as of eight years ago. The Eye sits in a cradle; the Orrery opens a clockwork iris over it at midnight on its own ('the lids'). THE EYE: while the lids are open it can be struck: bludgeoning or piercing only, and it's small, hard and glassy, perhaps as hard to hit as a knight in plate. Anyone in the Heart without a smoked-glass visor when the iris opens will begin to turn to stone. A Warden's gala visor will do. At the foot, underlined: 'This is how it was EIGHT YEARS AGO. She has had eight years to change it. Look before you leap. T.F.'
inventory.name: Tobias's Notes on the Blink and the Heart
inventory.source: gift: written by Tobias Fenwick in exchange for the Codex

inventory.description: Six close-written pages torn from the back of a spellbook, in a small, furious hand with diagrams. THE BLINK: at the Grand Conjunction the Orrery's last ring locks at the stroke of midnight, and the whole ward lattice goes dead for about three minutes and ten seconds. Every sigil plate, every alarm chime, and the Curator's own plate at the Undercroft door all go dark. The Brass Wardens are bound to the lattice and SHOULD stand still for the Blink ('should' underlined twice). THE HEART: a brass focal chamber in the Orrery works, directly under the great lens. Reach it by the Staff Only stair from the Rotunda, or from the Undercroft side. One door, as of eight years ago. The Eye sits in a cradle; the Orrery opens a clockwork iris over it at midnight on its own ('the lids'). THE EYE: while the lids are open it can be struck: bludgeoning or piercing only, and it's small, hard and glassy, perhaps as hard to hit as a knight in plate. Anyone in the Heart without a smoked-glass visor when the iris opens will begin to turn to stone. A Warden's gala visor will do. At the foot, underlined: 'This is how it was EIGHT YEARS AGO. She has had eight years to change it. Look before you leap. T.F.'

inventory.description: A single sheet, soft at the folds, in a quick slanting hand. Dated six years ago, five days before Emeric died. 'Wyn, love, they're running tests in the Hall of Heroes at night with the lamps out. Twice now I've seen a green light under the Rotunda doors, and the next week there's a new statue in the Hall and a name gone off the duty roll. Captain Thorne asked me to look away. He says it's the Curator's business and none of ours. I won't. If anything happens to me, it wasn't thieves and it wasn't an accident, whatever they tell you. Burn this. I know you won't. E.'
inventory.name: Emeric Dane's Last Letter
inventory.source: gift: lent by Wynn Dane to 'the chapel' for the Saint's Book of Remembrance; she wants it back

inventory.description: Six close-written pages torn from the back of a spellbook, in a small, furious hand with diagrams. THE BLINK: at the Grand Conjunction the Orrery's last ring locks at the stroke of midnight, and the whole ward lattice goes dead for about three minutes and ten seconds. Every sigil plate, every alarm chime, and the Curator's own plate at the Undercroft door all go dark. The Brass Wardens are bound to the lattice and SHOULD stand still for the Blink ('should' underlined twice). THE HEART: a brass focal chamber in the Orrery works, directly under the great lens. Reach it by the Staff Only stair from the Rotunda, or from the Undercroft side. One door, as of eight years ago. The Eye sits in a cradle; the Orrery opens a clockwork iris over it at midnight on its own ('the lids'). THE EYE: while the lids are open it can be struck: bludgeoning or piercing only, and it's small, hard and glassy, perhaps as hard to hit as a knight in plate. Anyone in the Heart without a smoked-glass visor when the iris opens will begin to turn to stone. A Warden's gala visor will do. At the foot, underlined: 'This is how it was EIGHT YEARS AGO. She has had eight years to change it. Look before you leap. T.F.'
inventory.name: Tobias's Notes on the Blink and the Heart
inventory.source: gift: written by Tobias Fenwick in exchange for the Codex

inventory.name: Dagger of Venom
inventory.note: Acquisitions exhibit A-148, lifted from its glass case in the Undercroft Stores. A slim blade of blued black steel with a green-enamelled hilt, faintly oily to the touch. A plain dagger lies on the black felt in its place, under an unbroken Acquisitions seal.

inventory.description: A single sheet, soft at the folds, in a quick slanting hand. Dated six years ago, five days before Emeric died. 'Wyn, love, they're running tests in the Hall of Heroes at night with the lamps out. Twice now I've seen a green light under the Rotunda doors, and the next week there's a new statue in the Hall and a name gone off the duty roll. Captain Thorne asked me to look away. He says it's the Curator's business and none of ours. I won't. If anything happens to me, it wasn't thieves and it wasn't an accident, whatever they tell you. Burn this. I know you won't. E.'
inventory.name: Emeric Dane's Last Letter
inventory.source: gift: lent by Wynn Dane to 'the chapel' for the Saint's Book of Remembrance; she wants it back

inventory.description: Six close-written pages torn from the back of a spellbook, in a small, furious hand with diagrams. THE BLINK: at the Grand Conjunction the Orrery's last ring locks at the stroke of midnight, and the whole ward lattice goes dead for about three minutes and ten seconds. Every sigil plate, every alarm chime, and the Curator's own plate at the Undercroft door all go dark. The Brass Wardens are bound to the lattice and SHOULD stand still for the Blink ('should' underlined twice). THE HEART: a brass focal chamber in the Orrery works, directly under the great lens. Reach it by the Staff Only stair from the Rotunda, or from the Undercroft side. One door, as of eight years ago. The Eye sits in a cradle; the Orrery opens a clockwork iris over it at midnight on its own ('the lids'). THE EYE: while the lids are open it can be struck: bludgeoning or piercing only, and it's small, hard and glassy, perhaps as hard to hit as a knight in plate. Anyone in the Heart without a smoked-glass visor when the iris opens will begin to turn to stone. A Warden's gala visor will do. At the foot, underlined: 'This is how it was EIGHT YEARS AGO. She has had eight years to change it. Look before you leap. T.F.'
inventory.name: Tobias's Notes on the Blink and the Heart
inventory.source: gift: written by Tobias Fenwick in exchange for the Codex

inventory.name: Dagger of Venom
inventory.note: Acquisitions exhibit A-148, lifted from its glass case in the Undercroft Stores. A slim blade of blued black steel with a green-enamelled hilt, faintly oily to the touch. A plain dagger lies on the black felt in its place, under an unbroken Acquisitions seal.
inventory.source: stolen: Acquisitions case A-148, Cage Three, Undercroft Stores (swapped for a plain dagger)

inventory.description: A small brass key stamped 9 on a loop of pink silk cord, for a changing-room cabinet at the Rosewater Baths. Loaned; to be returned on leaving.

item.description: Six close-written pages torn from the back of a spellbook, in a small, furious hand with diagrams. THE BLINK: at the Grand Conjunction the Orrery's last ring locks at the stroke of midnight, and the whole ward lattice goes dead for about three minutes and ten seconds. Every sigil plate, every alarm chime, and the Curator's own plate at the Undercroft door all go dark. The Brass Wardens are bound to the lattice and SHOULD stand still for the Blink ('should' underlined twice). THE HEART: a brass focal chamber in the Orrery works, directly under the great lens. Reach it by the Staff Only stair from the Rotunda, or from the Undercroft side. One door, as of eight years ago. The Eye sits in a cradle; the Orrery opens a clockwork iris over it at midnight on its own ('the lids'). THE EYE: while the lids are open it can be struck: bludgeoning or piercing only, and it's small, hard and glassy, perhaps as hard to hit as a knight in plate. Anyone in the Heart without a smoked-glass visor when the iris opens will begin to turn to stone. A Warden's gala visor will do. At the foot, underlined: 'This is how it was EIGHT YEARS AGO. She has had eight years to change it. Look before you leap. T.F.'
item.name: Tobias's Notes on the Blink and the Heart
item.source: gift: written by Tobias Fenwick in exchange for the Codex

item.description: Six close-written pages torn from the back of a spellbook, in a small, furious hand with diagrams. THE BLINK: at the Grand Conjunction the Orrery's last ring locks at the stroke of midnight, and the whole ward lattice goes dead for about three minutes and ten seconds. Every sigil plate, every alarm chime, and the Curator's own plate at the Undercroft door all go dark. The Brass Wardens are bound to the lattice and SHOULD stand still for the Blink ('should' underlined twice). THE HEART: a brass focal chamber in the Orrery works, directly under the great lens. Reach it by the Staff Only stair from the Rotunda, or from the Undercroft side. One door, as of eight years ago. The Eye sits in a cradle; the Orrery opens a clockwork iris over it at midnight on its own ('the lids'). THE EYE: while the lids are open it can be struck: bludgeoning or piercing only, and it's small, hard and glassy, perhaps as hard to hit as a knight in plate. Anyone in the Heart without a smoked-glass visor when the iris opens will begin to turn to stone. A Warden's gala visor will do. At the foot, underlined: 'This is how it was EIGHT YEARS AGO. She has had eight years to change it. Look before you leap. T.F.'
item.name: Tobias's Notes on the Blink and the Heart
item.source: gift: written by Tobias Fenwick in exchange for the Codex

item.description: Six close-written pages torn from the back of a spellbook, in a small, furious hand with diagrams. THE BLINK: at the Grand Conjunction the Orrery's last ring locks at the stroke of midnight, and the whole ward lattice goes dead for about three minutes and ten seconds. Every sigil plate, every alarm chime, and the Curator's own plate at the Undercroft door all go dark. The Brass Wardens are bound to the lattice and SHOULD stand still for the Blink ('should' underlined twice). THE HEART: a brass focal chamber in the Orrery works, directly under the great lens. Reach it by the Staff Only stair from the Rotunda, or from the Undercroft side. One door, as of eight years ago. The Eye sits in a cradle; the Orrery opens a clockwork iris over it at midnight on its own ('the lids'). THE EYE: while the lids are open it can be struck: bludgeoning or piercing only, and it's small, hard and glassy, perhaps as hard to hit as a knight in plate. Anyone in the Heart without a smoked-glass visor when the iris opens will begin to turn to stone. A Warden's gala visor will do. At the foot, underlined: 'This is how it was EIGHT YEARS AGO. She has had eight years to change it. Look before you leap. T.F.'
item.name: Tobias's Notes on the Blink and the Heart
item.source: gift: written by Tobias Fenwick in exchange for the Codex

He says it's the Curator's business and none of ours. I won't. If anything happens to me, it wasn't thieves and it wasn't an accident, whatever they tell you. Burn this. I know you won't. E.'

item.description: Six close-written pages torn from the back of a spellbook, in a small, furious hand with diagrams. THE BLINK: at the Grand Conjunction the Orrery's last ring locks at the stroke of midnight, and the whole ward lattice goes dead for about three minutes and ten seconds. Every sigil plate, every alarm chime, and the Curator's own plate at the Undercroft door all go dark. The Brass Wardens are bound to the lattice and SHOULD stand still for the Blink ('should' underlined twice). THE HEART: a brass focal chamber in the Orrery works, directly under the great lens. Reach it by the Staff Only stair from the Rotunda, or from the Undercroft side. One door, as of eight years ago. The Eye sits in a cradle; the Orrery opens a clockwork iris over it at midnight on its own ('the lids'). THE EYE: while the lids are open it can be struck: bludgeoning or piercing only, and it's small, hard and glassy, perhaps as hard to hit as a knight in plate. Anyone in the Heart without a smoked-glass visor when the iris opens will begin to turn to stone. A Warden's gala visor will do. At the foot, underlined: 'This is how it was EIGHT YEARS AGO. She has had eight years to change it. Look before you leap. T.F.'
item.name: Tobias's Notes on the Blink and the Heart
item.source: gift: written by Tobias Fenwick in exchange for the Codex

item.description: Six close-written pages torn from the back of a spellbook, in a small, furious hand with diagrams. THE BLINK: at the Grand Conjunction the Orrery's last ring locks at the stroke of midnight, and the whole ward lattice goes dead for about three minutes and ten seconds. Every sigil plate, every alarm chime, and the Curator's own plate at the Undercroft door all go dark. The Brass Wardens are bound to the lattice and SHOULD stand still for the Blink ('should' underlined twice). THE HEART: a brass focal chamber in the Orrery works, directly under the great lens. Reach it by the Staff Only stair from the Rotunda, or from the Undercroft side. One door, as of eight years ago. The Eye sits in a cradle; the Orrery opens a clockwork iris over it at midnight on its own ('the lids'). THE EYE: while the lids are open it can be struck: bludgeoning or piercing only, and it's small, hard and glassy, perhaps as hard to hit as a knight in plate. Anyone in the Heart without a smoked-glass visor when the iris opens will begin to turn to stone. A Warden's gala visor will do. At the foot, underlined: 'This is how it was EIGHT YEARS AGO. She has had eight years to change it. Look before you leap. T.F.'
item.name: Tobias's Notes on the Blink and the Heart
item.source: gift: written by Tobias Fenwick in exchange for the Codex

item.description: Six close-written pages torn from the back of a spellbook, in a small, furious hand with diagrams. THE BLINK: at the Grand Conjunction the Orrery's last ring locks at the stroke of midnight, and the whole ward lattice goes dead for about three minutes and ten seconds. Every sigil plate, every alarm chime, and the Curator's own plate at the Undercroft door all go dark. The Brass Wardens are bound to the lattice and SHOULD stand still for the Blink ('should' underlined twice). THE HEART: a brass focal chamber in the Orrery works, directly under the great lens. Reach it by the Staff Only stair from the Rotunda, or from the Undercroft side. One door, as of eight years ago. The Eye sits in a cradle; the Orrery opens a clockwork iris over it at midnight on its own ('the lids'). THE EYE: while the lids are open it can be struck: bludgeoning or piercing only, and it's small, hard and glassy, perhaps as hard to hit as a knight in plate. Anyone in the Heart without a smoked-glass visor when the iris opens will begin to turn to stone. A Warden's gala visor will do. At the foot, underlined: 'This is how it was EIGHT YEARS AGO. She has had eight years to change it. Look before you leap. T.F.'
item.name: Tobias's Notes on the Blink and the Heart

item.description: Six close-written pages torn from the back of a spellbook, in a small, furious hand with diagrams. THE BLINK: at the Grand Conjunction the Orrery's last ring locks at the stroke of midnight, and the whole ward lattice goes dead for about three minutes and ten seconds. Every sigil plate, every alarm chime, and the Curator's own plate at the Undercroft door all go dark. The Brass Wardens are bound to the lattice and SHOULD stand still for the Blink ('should' underlined twice). THE HEART: a brass focal chamber in the Orrery works, directly under the great lens. Reach it by the Staff Only stair from the Rotunda, or from the Undercroft side. One door, as of eight years ago. The Eye sits in a cradle; the Orrery opens a clockwork iris over it at midnight on its own ('the lids'). THE EYE: while the lids are open it can be struck: bludgeoning or piercing only, and it's small, hard and glassy, perhaps as hard to hit as a knight in plate. Anyone in the Heart without a smoked-glass visor when the iris opens will begin to turn to stone. A Warden's gala visor will do. At the foot, underlined: 'This is how it was EIGHT YEARS AGO. She has had eight years to change it. Look before you leap. T.F.'
item.name: Tobias's Notes on the Blink and the Heart
item.source: gift: written by Tobias Fenwick in exchange for the Codex

inventory.description: Six close-written pages torn from the back of a spellbook, in a small, furious hand with diagrams. THE BLINK: at the Grand Conjunction the Orrery's last ring locks at the stroke of midnight, and the whole ward lattice goes dead for about three minutes and ten seconds. Every sigil plate, every alarm chime, and the Curator's own plate at the Undercroft door all go dark. The Brass Wardens are bound to the lattice and SHOULD stand still for the Blink ('should' underlined twice). THE HEART: a brass focal chamber in the Orrery works, directly under the great lens. Reach it by the Staff Only stair from the Rotunda, or from the Undercroft side. One door, as of eight years ago. The Eye sits in a cradle; the Orrery opens a clockwork iris over it at midnight on its own ('the lids'). THE EYE: while the lids are open it can be struck: bludgeoning or piercing only, and it's small, hard and glassy, perhaps as hard to hit as a knight in plate. Anyone in the Heart without a smoked-glass visor when the iris opens will begin to turn to stone. A Warden's gala visor will do. At the foot, underlined: 'This is how it was EIGHT YEARS AGO. She has had eight years to change it. Look before you leap. T.F.'

inventory.description: A single sheet, soft at the folds, in a quick slanting hand. Dated six years ago, five days before Emeric died. 'Wyn, love, they're running tests in the Hall of Heroes at night with the lamps out. Twice now I've seen a green light under the Rotunda doors, and the next week there's a new statue in the Hall and a name gone off the duty roll. Captain Thorne asked me to look away. He says it's the Curator's business and none of ours. I won't. If anything happens to me, it wasn't thieves and it wasn't an accident, whatever they tell you. Burn this. I know you won't. E.'

inventory.description: Six close-written pages torn from the back of a spellbook, in a small, furious hand with diagrams. THE BLINK: at the Grand Conjunction the Orrery's last ring locks at the stroke of midnight, and the whole ward lattice goes dead for about three minutes and ten seconds. Every sigil plate, every alarm chime, and the Curator's own plate at the Undercroft door all go dark. The Brass Wardens are bound to the lattice and SHOULD stand still for the Blink ('should' underlined twice). THE HEART: a brass focal chamber in the Orrery works, directly under the great lens. Reach it by the Staff Only stair from the Rotunda, or from the Undercroft side. One door, as of eight years ago. The Eye sits in a cradle; the Orrery opens a clockwork iris over it at midnight on its own ('the lids'). THE EYE: while the lids are open it can be struck: bludgeoning or piercing only, and it's small, hard and glassy, perhaps as hard to hit as a knight in plate. Anyone in the Heart without a smoked-glass visor when the iris opens will begin to turn to stone. A Warden's gala visor will do. At the foot, underlined: 'This is how it was EIGHT YEARS AGO. She has had eight years to change it. Look before you leap. T.F.'
inventory.name: Tobias's Notes on the Blink and the Heart
inventory.source: gift: written by Tobias Fenwick in exchange for the Codex

inventory.description: A single sheet, soft at the folds, in a quick slanting hand. Dated six years ago, five days before Emeric died. 'Wyn, love, they're running tests in the Hall of Heroes at night with the lamps out. Twice now I've seen a green light under the Rotunda doors, and the next week there's a new statue in the Hall and a name gone off the duty roll. Captain Thorne asked me to look away. He says it's the Curator's business and none of ours. I won't. If anything happens to me, it wasn't thieves and it wasn't an accident, whatever they tell you. Burn this. I know you won't. E.'

inventory.description: Six close-written pages torn from the back of a spellbook, in a small, furious hand with diagrams. THE BLINK: at the Grand Conjunction the Orrery's last ring locks at the stroke of midnight, and the whole ward lattice goes dead for about three minutes and ten seconds. Every sigil plate, every alarm chime, and the Curator's own plate at the Undercroft door all go dark. The Brass Wardens are bound to the lattice and SHOULD stand still for the Blink ('should' underlined twice). THE HEART: a brass focal chamber in the Orrery works, directly under the great lens. Reach it by the Staff Only stair from the Rotunda, or from the Undercroft side. One door, as of eight years ago. The Eye sits in a cradle; the Orrery opens a clockwork iris over it at midnight on its own ('the lids'). THE EYE: while the lids are open it can be struck: bludgeoning or piercing only, and it's small, hard and glassy, perhaps as hard to hit as a knight in plate. Anyone in the Heart without a smoked-glass visor when the iris opens will begin to turn to stone. A Warden's gala visor will do. At the foot, underlined: 'This is how it was EIGHT YEARS AGO. She has had eight years to change it. Look before you leap. T.F.'
inventory.name: Tobias's Notes on the Blink and the Heart
inventory.source: gift: written by Tobias Fenwick in exchange for the Codex

inventory.description: A single sheet, soft at the folds, in a quick slanting hand. Dated six years ago, five days before Emeric died. 'Wyn, love, they're running tests in the Hall of Heroes at night with the lamps out. Twice now I've seen a green light under the Rotunda doors, and the next week there's a new statue in the Hall and a name gone off the duty roll. Captain Thorne asked me to look away. He says it's the Curator's business and none of ours. I won't. If anything happens to me, it wasn't thieves and it wasn't an accident, whatever they tell you. Burn this. I know you won't. E.'
inventory.name: Emeric Dane's Last Letter
inventory.source: gift: lent by Wynn Dane to 'the chapel' for the Saint's Book of Remembrance; she wants it back

inventory.description: Six close-written pages torn from the back of a spellbook, in a small, furious hand with diagrams. THE BLINK: at the Grand Conjunction the Orrery's last ring locks at the stroke of midnight, and the whole ward lattice goes dead for about three minutes and ten seconds. Every sigil plate, every alarm chime, and the Curator's own plate at the Undercroft door all go dark. The Brass Wardens are bound to the lattice and SHOULD stand still for the Blink ('should' underlined twice). THE HEART: a brass focal chamber in the Orrery works, directly under the great lens. Reach it by the Staff Only stair from the Rotunda, or from the Undercroft side. One door, as of eight years ago. The Eye sits in a cradle; the Orrery opens a clockwork iris over it at midnight on its own ('the lids'). THE EYE: while the lids are open it can be struck: bludgeoning or piercing only, and it's small, hard and glassy, perhaps as hard to hit as a knight in plate. Anyone in the Heart without a smoked-glass visor when the iris opens will begin to turn to stone. A Warden's gala visor will do. At the foot, underlined: 'This is how it was EIGHT YEARS AGO. She has had eight years to change it. Look before you leap. T.F.'
inventory.name: Tobias's Notes on the Blink and the Heart
inventory.source: gift: written by Tobias Fenwick in exchange for the Codex

inventory.description: A heavy gold hunter-case watch on a short chain. The lid is engraved with a bunch of grapes and 'B.P. from M., with love'. It still ticks. A fence would pay perhaps 25 gp; it's worth more to Pell.
inventory.name: Gold pocket watch

inventory.description: Six close-written pages torn from the back of a spellbook, in a small, furious hand with diagrams. THE BLINK: at the Grand Conjunction the Orrery's last ring locks at the stroke of midnight, and the whole ward lattice goes dead for about three minutes and ten seconds. Every sigil plate, every alarm chime, and the Curator's own plate at the Undercroft door all go dark. The Brass Wardens are bound to the lattice and SHOULD stand still for the Blink ('should' underlined twice). THE HEART: a brass focal chamber in the Orrery works, directly under the great lens. Reach it by the Staff Only stair from the Rotunda, or from the Undercroft side. One door, as of eight years ago. The Eye sits in a cradle; the Orrery opens a clockwork iris over it at midnight on its own ('the lids'). THE EYE: while the lids are open it can be struck: bludgeoning or piercing only, and it's small, hard and glassy, perhaps as hard to hit as a knight in plate. Anyone in the Heart without a smoked-glass visor when the iris opens will begin to turn to stone. A Warden's gala visor will do. At the foot, underlined: 'This is how it was EIGHT YEARS AGO. She has had eight years to change it. Look before you leap. T.F.'
inventory.name: Tobias's Notes on the Blink and the Heart
inventory.source: gift: written by Tobias Fenwick in exchange for the Codex

inventory.description: Six close-written pages torn from the back of a spellbook, in a small, furious hand with diagrams. THE BLINK: at the Grand Conjunction the Orrery's last ring locks at the stroke of midnight, and the whole ward lattice goes dead for about three minutes and ten seconds. Every sigil plate, every alarm chime, and the Curator's own plate at the Undercroft door all go dark. The Brass Wardens are bound to the lattice and SHOULD stand still for the Blink ('should' underlined twice). THE HEART: a brass focal chamber in the Orrery works, directly under the great lens. Reach it by the Staff Only stair from the Rotunda, or from the Undercroft side. One door, as of eight years ago. The Eye sits in a cradle; the Orrery opens a clockwork iris over it at midnight on its own ('the lids'). THE EYE: while the lids are open it can be struck: bludgeoning or piercing only, and it's small, hard and glassy, perhaps as hard to hit as a knight in plate. Anyone in the Heart without a smoked-glass visor when the iris opens will begin to turn to stone. A Warden's gala visor will do. At the foot, underlined: 'This is how it was EIGHT YEARS AGO. She has had eight years to change it. Look before you leap. T.F.'
inventory.name: Tobias's Notes on the Blink and the Heart
inventory.source: gift: written by Tobias Fenwick in exchange for the Codex

inventory.description: A single sheet, soft at the folds, in a quick slanting hand. Dated six years ago, five days before Emeric died. 'Wyn, love, they're running tests in the Hall of Heroes at night with the lamps out. Twice now I've seen a green light under the Rotunda doors, and the next week there's a new statue in the Hall and a name gone off the duty roll. Captain Thorne asked me to look away. He says it's the Curator's business and none of ours. I won't. If anything happens to me, it wasn't thieves and it wasn't an accident, whatever they tell you. Burn this. I know you won't. E.'
inventory.name: Emeric Dane's Last Letter
inventory.source: gift: lent by Wynn Dane to 'the chapel' for the Saint's Book of Remembrance; she wants it back

inventory.description: Six close-written pages torn from the back of a spellbook, in a small, furious hand with diagrams. THE BLINK: at the Grand Conjunction the Orrery's last ring locks at the stroke of midnight, and the whole ward lattice goes dead for about three minutes and ten seconds. Every sigil plate, every alarm chime, and the Curator's own plate at the Undercroft door all go dark. The Brass Wardens are bound to the lattice and SHOULD stand still for the Blink ('should' underlined twice). THE HEART: a brass focal chamber in the Orrery works, directly under the great lens. Reach it by the Staff Only stair from the Rotunda, or from the Undercroft side. One door, as of eight years ago. The Eye sits in a cradle; the Orrery opens a clockwork iris over it at midnight on its own ('the lids'). THE EYE: while the lids are open it can be struck: bludgeoning or piercing only, and it's small, hard and glassy, perhaps as hard to hit as a knight in plate. Anyone in the Heart without a smoked-glass visor when the iris opens will begin to turn to stone. A Warden's gala visor will do. At the foot, underlined: 'This is how it was EIGHT YEARS AGO. She has had eight years to change it. Look before you leap. T.F.'
inventory.name: Tobias's Notes on the Blink and the Heart
inventory.source: gift: written by Tobias Fenwick in exchange for the Codex

inventory.description: A folded order on the Meridian's cream letter-paper, sealed with the museum's orrery stamp: 'Pellow & Sons, Vintner's Row. inventory.description: Six close-written pages torn from the back of a spellbook, in a small, furious hand with diagrams. THE BLINK: at the Grand Conjunction the Orrery's last ring locks at the stroke of midnight, and the whole ward lattice goes dead for about three minutes and ten seconds. Every sigil plate, every alarm chime, and the Curator's own plate at the Undercroft door all go dark. The Brass Wardens are bound to the lattice and SHOULD stand still for the Blink ('should' underlined twice). THE HEART: a brass focal chamber in the Orrery works, directly under the great lens. Reach it by the Staff Only stair from the Rotunda, or from the Undercroft side. One door, as of eight years ago. The Eye sits in a cradle; the Orrery opens a clockwork iris over it at midnight on its own ('the lids'). THE EYE: while the lids are open it can be struck: bludgeoning or piercing only, and it's small, hard and glassy, perhaps as hard to hit as a knight in plate. Anyone in the Heart without a smoked-glass visor when the iris opens will begin to turn to stone. A Warden's gala visor will do. At the foot, underlined: 'This is how it was EIGHT YEARS AGO. She has had eight years to change it. Look before you leap. T.F.'
inventory.name: Tobias's Notes on the Blink and the Heart
inventory.source: gift: written by Tobias Fenwick in exchange for the Codex

inventory.description: A single sheet, soft at the folds, in a quick slanting hand. Dated six years ago, five days before Emeric died. 'Wyn, love, they're running tests in the Hall of Heroes at night with the lamps out. Twice now I've seen a green light under the Rotunda doors, and the next week there's a new statue in the Hall and a name gone off the duty roll. Captain Thorne asked me to look away. He says it's the Curator's business and none of ours. I won't. If anything happens to me, it wasn't thieves and it wasn't an accident, whatever they tell you. Burn this. I know you won't. E.'
inventory.name: Emeric Dane's Last Letter
inventory.source: gift: lent by Wynn Dane to 'the chapel' for the Saint's Book of Remembrance; she wants it back

inventory.description: Six close-written pages torn from the back of a spellbook, in a small, furious hand with diagrams. THE BLINK: at the Grand Conjunction the Orrery's last ring locks at the stroke of midnight, and the whole ward lattice goes dead for about three minutes and ten seconds. Every sigil plate, every alarm chime, and the Curator's own plate at the Undercroft door all go dark. The Brass Wardens are bound to the lattice and SHOULD stand still for the Blink ('should' underlined twice). THE HEART: a brass focal chamber in the Orrery works, directly under the great lens. Reach it by the Staff Only stair from the Rotunda, or from the Undercroft side. One door, as of eight years ago. The Eye sits in a cradle; the Orrery opens a clockwork iris over it at midnight on its own ('the lids'). THE EYE: while the lids are open it can be struck: bludgeoning or piercing only, and it's small, hard and glassy, perhaps as hard to hit as a knight in plate. Anyone in the Heart without a smoked-glass visor when the iris opens will begin to turn to stone. A Warden's gala visor will do. At the foot, underlined: 'This is how it was EIGHT YEARS AGO. She has had eight years to change it. Look before you leap. T.F.'
inventory.name: Tobias's Notes on the Blink and the Heart
inventory.source: gift: written by Tobias Fenwick in exchange for the Codex

inventory.description: Six close-written pages torn from the back of a spellbook, in a small, furious hand with diagrams. THE BLINK: at the Grand Conjunction the Orrery's last ring locks at the stroke of midnight, and the whole ward lattice goes dead for about three minutes and ten seconds. Every sigil plate, every alarm chime, and the Curator's own plate at the Undercroft door all go dark. The Brass Wardens are bound to the lattice and SHOULD stand still for the Blink ('should' underlined twice). THE HEART: a brass focal chamber in the Orrery works, directly under the great lens. Reach it by the Staff Only stair from the Rotunda, or from the Undercroft side. One door, as of eight years ago. The Eye sits in a cradle; the Orrery opens a clockwork iris over it at midnight on its own ('the lids'). THE EYE: while the lids are open it can be struck: bludgeoning or piercing only, and it's small, hard and glassy, perhaps as hard to hit as a knight in plate. Anyone in the Heart without a smoked-glass visor when the iris opens will begin to turn to stone. A Warden's gala visor will do. At the foot, underlined: 'This is how it was EIGHT YEARS AGO. She has had eight years to change it. Look before you leap. T.F.'
inventory.name: Tobias's Notes on the Blink and the Heart
inventory.source: gift: written by Tobias Fenwick in exchange for the Codex

inventory.description: A single sheet, soft at the folds, in a quick slanting hand. Dated six years ago, five days before Emeric died. 'Wyn, love, they're running tests in the Hall of Heroes at night with the lamps out. Twice now I've seen a green light under the Rotunda doors, and the next week there's a new statue in the Hall and a name gone off the duty roll. Captain Thorne asked me to look away. He says it's the Curator's business and none of ours. I won't. If anything happens to me, it wasn't thieves and it wasn't an accident, whatever they tell you. Burn this. I know you won't. E.'

inventory.source: gift: lent by Wynn Dane to 'the chapel' for the Saint's Book of Remembrance; she wants it back

inventory.description: Six close-written pages torn from the back of a spellbook, in a small, furious hand with diagrams. THE BLINK: at the Grand Conjunction the Orrery's last ring locks at the stroke of midnight, and the whole ward lattice goes dead for about three minutes and ten seconds. Every sigil plate, every alarm chime, and the Curator's own plate at the Undercroft door all go dark. The Brass Wardens are bound to the lattice and SHOULD stand still for the Blink ('should' underlined twice). THE HEART: a brass focal chamber in the Orrery works, directly under the great lens. Reach it by the Staff Only stair from the Rotunda, or from the Undercroft side. One door, as of eight years ago. The Eye sits in a cradle; the Orrery opens a clockwork iris over it at midnight on its own ('the lids'). THE EYE: while the lids are open it can be struck: bludgeoning or piercing only, and it's small, hard and glassy, perhaps as hard to hit as a knight in plate. Anyone in the Heart without a smoked-glass visor when the iris opens will begin to turn to stone. A Warden's gala visor will do. At the foot, underlined: 'This is how it was EIGHT YEARS AGO. She has had eight years to change it. Look before you leap. T.F.'
inventory.name: Tobias's Notes on the Blink and the Heart
inventory.source: gift: written by Tobias Fenwick in exchange for the Codex

inventory.description: Six close-written pages torn from the back of a spellbook, in a small, furious hand with diagrams. THE BLINK: at the Grand Conjunction the Orrery's last ring locks at the stroke of midnight, and the whole ward lattice goes dead for about three minutes and ten seconds. Every sigil plate, every alarm chime, and the Curator's own plate at the Undercroft door all go dark. The Brass Wardens are bound to the lattice and SHOULD stand still for the Blink ('should' underlined twice). THE HEART: a brass focal chamber in the Orrery works, directly under the great lens. Reach it by the Staff Only stair from the Rotunda, or from the Undercroft side. One door, as of eight years ago. The Eye sits in a cradle; the Orrery opens a clockwork iris over it at midnight on its own ('the lids'). THE EYE: while the lids are open it can be struck: bludgeoning or piercing only, and it's small, hard and glassy, perhaps as hard to hit as a knight in plate. Anyone in the Heart without a smoked-glass visor when the iris opens will begin to turn to stone. A Warden's gala visor will do. At the foot, underlined: 'This is how it was EIGHT YEARS AGO. She has had eight years to change it. Look before you leap. T.F.'

inventory.description: Six close-written pages torn from the back of a spellbook, in a small, furious hand with diagrams. THE BLINK: at the Grand Conjunction the Orrery's last ring locks at the stroke of midnight, and the whole ward lattice goes dead for about three minutes and ten seconds. Every sigil plate, every alarm chime, and the Curator's own plate at the Undercroft door all go dark. The Brass Wardens are bound to the lattice and SHOULD stand still for the Blink ('should' underlined twice). THE HEART: a brass focal chamber in the Orrery works, directly under the great lens. Reach it by the Staff Only stair from the Rotunda, or from the Undercroft side. One door, as of eight years ago. The Eye sits in a cradle; the Orrery opens a clockwork iris over it at midnight on its own ('the lids'). THE EYE: while the lids are open it can be struck: bludgeoning or piercing only, and it's small, hard and glassy, perhaps as hard to hit as a knight in plate. Anyone in the Heart without a smoked-glass visor when the iris opens will begin to turn to stone. A Warden's gala visor will do. At the foot, underlined: 'This is how it was EIGHT YEARS AGO. She has had eight years to change it. Look before you leap. T.F.'
inventory.name: Tobias's Notes on the Blink and the Heart
inventory.source: gift: written by Tobias Fenwick in exchange for the Codex

inventory.description: A single sheet, soft at the folds, in a quick slanting hand. Dated six years ago, five days before Emeric died. 'Wyn, love, they're running tests in the Hall of Heroes at night with the lamps out. Twice now I've seen a green light under the Rotunda doors, and the next week there's a new statue in the Hall and a name gone off the duty roll. Captain Thorne asked me to look away. He says it's the Curator's business and none of ours. I won't. If anything happens to me, it wasn't thieves and it wasn't an accident, whatever they tell you. Burn this. I know you won't. E.'
inventory.name: Emeric Dane's Last Letter
inventory.source: gift: lent by Wynn Dane to 'the chapel' for the Saint's Book of Remembrance; she wants it back

inventory.description: Six close-written pages torn from the back of a spellbook, in a small, furious hand with diagrams. THE BLINK: at the Grand Conjunction the Orrery's last ring locks at the stroke of midnight, and the whole ward lattice goes dead for about three minutes and ten seconds. Every sigil plate, every alarm chime, and the Curator's own plate at the Undercroft door all go dark. The Brass Wardens are bound to the lattice and SHOULD stand still for the Blink ('should' underlined twice). THE HEART: a brass focal chamber in the Orrery works, directly under the great lens. Reach it by the Staff Only stair from the Rotunda, or from the Undercroft side. One door, as of eight years ago. The Eye sits in a cradle; the Orrery opens a clockwork iris over it at midnight on its own ('the lids'). THE EYE: while the lids are open it can be struck: bludgeoning or piercing only, and it's small, hard and glassy, perhaps as hard to hit as a knight in plate. Anyone in the Heart without a smoked-glass visor when the iris opens will begin to turn to stone. A Warden's gala visor will do. At the foot, underlined: 'This is how it was EIGHT YEARS AGO. She has had eight years to change it. Look before you leap. T.F.'
inventory.name: Tobias's Notes on the Blink and the Heart
inventory.source: gift: written by Tobias Fenwick in exchange for the Codex

inventory.description: A single sheet, soft at the folds, in a quick slanting hand. Dated six years ago, five days before Emeric died. 'Wyn, love, they're running tests in the Hall of Heroes at night with the lamps out. Twice now I've seen a green light under the Rotunda doors, and the next week there's a new statue in the Hall and a name gone off the duty roll. Captain Thorne asked me to look away. He says it's the Curator's business and none of ours. I won't. If anything happens to me, it wasn't thieves and it wasn't an accident, whatever they tell you. Burn this. I know you won't. E.'
inventory.name: Emeric Dane's Last Letter
inventory.source: gift: lent by Wynn Dane to 'the chapel' for the Saint's Book of Remembrance; she wants it back

inventory.description: Six close-written pages torn from the back of a spellbook, in a small, furious hand with diagrams. THE BLINK: at the Grand Conjunction the Orrery's last ring locks at the stroke of midnight, and the whole ward lattice goes dead for about three minutes and ten seconds. Every sigil plate, every alarm chime, and the Curator's own plate at the Undercroft door all go dark. The Brass Wardens are bound to the lattice and SHOULD stand still for the Blink ('should' underlined twice). THE HEART: a brass focal chamber in the Orrery works, directly under the great lens. Reach it by the Staff Only stair from the Rotunda, or from the Undercroft side. One door, as of eight years ago. The Eye sits in a cradle; the Orrery opens a clockwork iris over it at midnight on its own ('the lids'). THE EYE: while the lids are open it can be struck: bludgeoning or piercing only, and it's small, hard and glassy, perhaps as hard to hit as a knight in plate. Anyone in the Heart without a smoked-glass visor when the iris opens will begin to turn to stone. A Warden's gala visor will do. At the foot, underlined: 'This is how it was EIGHT YEARS AGO. She has had eight years to change it. Look before you leap. T.F.'
inventory.name: Tobias's Notes on the Blink and the Heart
inventory.source: gift: written by Tobias Fenwick in exchange for the Codex

inventory.description: A folded order on the Meridian's cream letter-paper, sealed with the museum's orrery stamp: 'Pellow & Sons, Vintner's Row. Present this order to the landing warden for admittance of the cart and one (1) porter. Signed, E. Marrow, Steward of the Household.'

inventory.description: Six close-written pages torn from the back of a spellbook, in a small, furious hand with diagrams. THE BLINK: at the Grand Conjunction the Orrery's last ring locks at the stroke of midnight, and the whole ward lattice goes dead for about three minutes and ten seconds. Every sigil plate, every alarm chime, and the Curator's own plate at the Undercroft door all go dark. The Brass Wardens are bound to the lattice and SHOULD stand still for the Blink ('should' underlined twice). THE HEART: a brass focal chamber in the Orrery works, directly under the great lens. Reach it by the Staff Only stair from the Rotunda, or from the Undercroft side. One door, as of eight years ago. The Eye sits in a cradle; the Orrery opens a clockwork iris over it at midnight on its own ('the lids'). THE EYE: while the lids are open it can be struck: bludgeoning or piercing only, and it's small, hard and glassy, perhaps as hard to hit as a knight in plate. Anyone in the Heart without a smoked-glass visor when the iris opens will begin to turn to stone. A Warden's gala visor will do. At the foot, underlined: 'This is how it was EIGHT YEARS AGO. She has had eight years to change it. Look before you leap. T.F.'
inventory.name: Tobias's Notes on the Blink and the Heart
inventory.source: gift: written by Tobias Fenwick in exchange for the Codex

'Wyn, love, they're running tests in the Hall of Heroes at night with the lamps out. inventory.description: Six close-written pages torn from the back of a spellbook, in a small, furious hand with diagrams. THE BLINK: at the Grand Conjunction the Orrery's last ring locks at the stroke of midnight, and the whole ward lattice goes dead for about three minutes and ten seconds. Every sigil plate, every alarm chime, and the Curator's own plate at the Undercroft door all go dark. The Brass Wardens are bound to the lattice and SHOULD stand still for the Blink ('should' underlined twice). THE HEART: a brass focal chamber in the Orrery works, directly under the great lens. Reach it by the Staff Only stair from the Rotunda, or from the Undercroft side. One door, as of eight years ago. The Eye sits in a cradle; the Orrery opens a clockwork iris over it at midnight on its own ('the lids'). THE EYE: while the lids are open it can be struck: bludgeoning or piercing only, and it's small, hard and glassy, perhaps as hard to hit as a knight in plate. Anyone in the Heart without a smoked-glass visor when the iris opens will begin to turn to stone. A Warden's gala visor will do. At the foot, underlined: 'This is how it was EIGHT YEARS AGO. She has had eight years to change it. Look before you leap. T.F.'
inventory.name: Tobias's Notes on the Blink and the Heart
inventory.source: gift: written by Tobias Fenwick in exchange for the Codex

'Wyn, love, they're running tests in the Hall of Heroes at night with the lamps out. inventory.description: Six close-written pages torn from the back of a spellbook, in a small, furious hand with diagrams. THE BLINK: at the Grand Conjunction the Orrery's last ring locks at the stroke of midnight, and the whole ward lattice goes dead for about three minutes and ten seconds. Every sigil plate, every alarm chime, and the Curator's own plate at the Undercroft door all go dark. The Brass Wardens are bound to the lattice and SHOULD stand still for the Blink ('should' underlined twice). THE HEART: a brass focal chamber in the Orrery works, directly under the great lens. Reach it by the Staff Only stair from the Rotunda, or from the Undercroft side. One door, as of eight years ago. The Eye sits in a cradle; the Orrery opens a clockwork iris over it at midnight on its own ('the lids'). THE EYE: while the lids are open it can be struck: bludgeoning or piercing only, and it's small, hard and glassy, perhaps as hard to hit as a knight in plate. Anyone in the Heart without a smoked-glass visor when the iris opens will begin to turn to stone. A Warden's gala visor will do. At the foot, underlined: 'This is how it was EIGHT YEARS AGO. She has had eight years to change it. Look before you leap. T.F.'
inventory.name: Tobias's Notes on the Blink and the Heart
inventory.source: gift: written by Tobias Fenwick in exchange for the Codex

THE EYE: while the lids are open it can be struck: bludgeoning or piercing only, and it's small, hard and glassy, perhaps as hard to hit as a knight in plate. Anyone in the Heart without a smoked-glass visor when the iris opens will begin to turn to stone. A Warden's gala visor will do. At the foot, underlined: 'This is how it was EIGHT YEARS AGO. She has had eight years to change it. Look before you leap. T.F.'

inventory.description: Six close-written pages torn from the back of a spellbook, in a small, furious hand with diagrams. THE BLINK: at the Grand Conjunction the Orrery's last ring locks at the stroke of midnight, and the whole ward lattice goes dead for about three minutes and ten seconds. Every sigil plate, every alarm chime, and the Curator's own plate at the Undercroft door all go dark. The Brass Wardens are bound to the lattice and SHOULD stand still for the Blink ('should' underlined twice). THE HEART: a brass focal chamber in the Orrery works, directly under the great lens. Reach it by the Staff Only stair from the Rotunda, or from the Undercroft side. One door, as of eight years ago. The Eye sits in a cradle; the Orrery opens a clockwork iris over it at midnight on its own ('the lids'). THE EYE: while the lids are open it can be struck: bludgeoning or piercing only, and it's small, hard and glassy, perhaps as hard to hit as a knight in plate. Anyone in the Heart without a smoked-glass visor when the iris opens will begin to turn to stone. A Warden's gala visor will do. At the foot, underlined: 'This is how it was EIGHT YEARS AGO. She has had eight years to change it. Look before you leap. T.F.'

inventory.description: Six close-written pages torn from the back of a spellbook, in a small, furious hand with diagrams. THE BLINK: at the Grand Conjunction the Orrery's last ring locks at the stroke of midnight, and the whole ward lattice goes dead for about three minutes and ten seconds. Every sigil plate, every alarm chime, and the Curator's own plate at the Undercroft door all go dark. The Brass Wardens are bound to the lattice and SHOULD stand still for the Blink ('should' underlined twice). THE HEART: a brass focal chamber in the Orrery works, directly under the great lens. Reach it by the Staff Only stair from the Rotunda, or from the Undercroft side. One door, as of eight years ago. The Eye sits in a cradle; the Orrery opens a clockwork iris over it at midnight on its own ('the lids'). THE EYE: while the lids are open it can be struck: bludgeoning or piercing only, and it's small, hard and glassy, perhaps as hard to hit as a knight in plate. Anyone in the Heart without a smoked-glass visor when the iris opens will begin to turn to stone. A Warden's gala visor will do. At the foot, underlined: 'This is how it was EIGHT YEARS AGO. She has had eight years to change it. Look before you leap. T.F.'

inventory.name: Forged Leave Request (Varga)
inventory.source: crafted: Sera's forgery (Calligrapher's Supplies 20 vs DC 15)

inventory.description: A heavy coin of dark gold stamped on both sides with a closed eye. The Emissary pays in these. Crane: 'He'll know it if he sees it.'
inventory.name: Black-Gold Coin
inventory.source: gift: Valentin Crane, from his waistcoat

inventory.description: Varga's Meridian Warden sigil: silver, stamped with the sun-and-key. Tuned to the museum's ward lattice. Passes the Bridge of Saints staff gate, the island's outer wards and the galleries after hours, but not the Orrery floor. It becomes an alarm once the Wardens strike Varga's name from their ledger.
inventory.name: Warden's Sigil Ring
inventory.source: stolen: pried off Sergeant Varga's chained hand in the Heron's brig

inventory.description: A single sheet, soft at the folds, in a quick slanting hand. Dated six years ago, five days before Emeric died. 'Wyn, love, they're running tests in the Hall of Heroes at night with the lamps out. Twice now I've seen a green light under the Rotunda doors, and the next week there's a new statue in the Hall and a name gone off the duty roll. Captain Thorne asked me to look away. He says it's the Curator's business and none of ours. I won't. If anything happens to me, it wasn't thieves and it wasn't an accident, whatever they tell you. Burn this. I know you won't. E.'
inventory.name: Emeric Dane's Last Letter
inventory.source: gift: lent by Wynn Dane to 'the chapel' for the Saint's Book of Remembrance; she wants it back

inventory.description: A folded order on the Meridian's cream letter-paper, sealed with the museum's orrery stamp: 'Pellow & Sons, Vintner's Row. Sixty (60) bottles, Sable Vine '31, for the Lantern Gala. Deliver the afternoon of the eighth day, third bell, to the SERVICE LANDING (east water-stairs). Present this order to the landing warden for admittance of the cart and one (1) porter. Signed, E. Marrow, Steward of the Household.'
inventory.name: Wine delivery order
inventory.source: stolen: coat pocket in Pell's cabinet 8, Rosewater Baths

inventory.description: Five iron and brass keys on a ring with a cork tag reading PELLOW & SONS - VINTNER'S ROW. Front door, cellar, counting-room, and two smaller cabinet keys.

inventory.description: A single sheet, soft at the folds, in a quick slanting hand. Dated six years ago, five days before Emeric died. 'Wyn, love, they're running tests in the Hall of Heroes at night with the lamps out. Twice now I've seen a green light under the Rotunda doors, and the next week there's a new statue in the Hall and a name gone off the duty roll. Captain Thorne asked me to look away. He says it's the Curator's business and none of ours. I won't. If anything happens to me, it wasn't thieves and it wasn't an accident, whatever they tell you. Burn this. I know you won't. E.'
inventory.name: Emeric Dane's Last Letter
inventory.source: gift: lent by Wynn Dane to 'the chapel' for the Saint's Book of Remembrance; she wants it back

inventory.description: A single sheet, soft at the folds, in a quick slanting hand. Dated six years ago, five days before Emeric died. 'Wyn, love, they're running tests in the Hall of Heroes at night with the lamps out. Twice now I've seen a green light under the Rotunda doors, and the next week there's a new statue in the Hall and a name gone off the duty roll. Captain Thorne asked me to look away. He says it's the Curator's business and none of ours. I won't. If anything happens to me, it wasn't thieves and it wasn't an accident, whatever they tell you. Burn this. I know you won't. E.'

inventory.description: A single sheet, soft at the folds, in a quick slanting hand. Dated six years ago, five days before Emeric died. 'Wyn, love, they're running tests in the Hall of Heroes at night with the lamps out. He says it's the Curator's business and none of ours. I won't. If anything happens to me, it wasn't thieves and it wasn't an accident, whatever they tell you. Burn this. I know you won't. E.'

inventory.description: Six close-written pages torn from the back of a spellbook, in a small, furious hand with diagrams. THE BLINK: at the Grand Conjunction the Orrery's last ring locks at the stroke of midnight, and the whole ward lattice goes dead for about three minutes and ten seconds. Every sigil plate, every alarm chime, and the Curator's own plate at the Undercroft door all go dark. The Brass Wardens are bound to the lattice and SHOULD stand still for the Blink ('should' underlined twice). THE HEART: a brass focal chamber in the Orrery works, directly under the great lens. Reach it by the Staff Only stair from the Rotunda, or from the Undercroft side. One door, as of eight years ago. The Eye sits in a cradle; the Orrery opens a clockwork iris over it at midnight on its own ('the lids'). THE EYE: while the lids are open it can be struck: bludgeoning or piercing only, and it's small, hard and glassy, perhaps as hard to hit as a knight in plate. Anyone in the Heart without a smoked-glass visor when the iris opens will begin to turn to stone. A Warden's gala visor will do. At the foot, underlined: 'This is how it was EIGHT YEARS AGO. She has had eight years to change it. Look before you leap. T.F.'
inventory.name: Tobias's Notes on the Blink and the Heart
inventory.source: gift: written by Tobias Fenwick in exchange for the Codex

inventory.note: Second-hand from Nance Pettle's rag stall: a long brown wool coat gone shiny at the elbows, a grey waistcoat, a flat cloth cap. A clerk's clothes, not a magister's.

inventory.name: Her ladyship's terms

inventory.description: A single sheet, soft at the folds, in a quick slanting hand. Dated six years ago, five days before Emeric died. 'Wyn, love, they're running tests in the Hall of Heroes at night with the lamps out. Twice now I've seen a green light under the Rotunda doors, and the next week there's a new statue in the Hall and a name gone off the duty roll. Captain Thorne asked me to look away. He says it's the Curator's business and none of ours. I won't. If anything happens to me, it wasn't thieves and it wasn't an accident, whatever they tell you. Burn this. I know you won't. E.'

inventory.description: Varga's Meridian Warden sigil: silver, stamped with the sun-and-key. Tuned to the museum's ward lattice. Passes the Bridge of Saints staff gate, the island's outer wards and the galleries after hours, but not the Orrery floor. It becomes an alarm once the Wardens strike Varga's name from their ledger.
inventory.name: Warden's Sigil Ring
inventory.source: stolen: pried off Sergeant Varga's chained hand in the Heron's brig

inventory.description: A single sheet, soft at the folds, in a quick slanting hand. Dated six years ago, five days before Emeric died. 'Wyn, love, they're running tests in the Hall of Heroes at night with the lamps out. Twice now I've seen a green light under the Rotunda doors, and the next week there's a new statue in the Hall and a name gone off the duty roll. Captain Thorne asked me to look away. He says it's the Curator's business and none of ours. I won't. If anything happens to me, it wasn't thieves and it wasn't an accident, whatever they tell you. Burn this. I know you won't. E.'
inventory.name: Emeric Dane's Last Letter
inventory.source: gift: lent by Wynn Dane to 'the chapel' for the Saint's Book of Remembrance; she wants it back

inventory.description: A folded order on the Meridian's cream letter-paper, sealed with the museum's orrery stamp: 'Pellow & Sons, Vintner's Row. Sixty (60) bottles, Sable Vine '31, for the Lantern Gala. Deliver the afternoon of the eighth day, third bell, to the SERVICE LANDING (east water-stairs). Present this order to the landing warden for admittance of the cart and one (1) porter. Signed, E. Marrow, Steward of the Household.'
inventory.name: Wine delivery order
inventory.source: stolen: coat pocket in Pell's cabinet 8, Rosewater Baths

inventory.source: stolen: pried off Sergeant Varga's chained hand in the Heron's brig

inventory.description: A single sheet, soft at the folds, in a quick slanting hand. Dated six years ago, five days before Emeric died. 'Wyn, love, they're running tests in the Hall of Heroes at night with the lamps out. Twice now I've seen a green light under the Rotunda doors, and the next week there's a new statue in the Hall and a name gone off the duty roll. Captain Thorne asked me to look away. He says it's the Curator's business and none of ours. I won't. If anything happens to me, it wasn't thieves and it wasn't an accident, whatever they tell you. Burn this. I know you won't. E.'
inventory.name: Emeric Dane's Last Letter
inventory.source: gift: lent by Wynn Dane to 'the chapel' for the Saint's Book of Remembrance; she wants it back

inventory.description: A folded order on the Meridian's cream letter-paper, sealed with the museum's orrery stamp: 'Pellow & Sons, Vintner's Row. Sixty (60) bottles, Sable Vine '31, for the Lantern Gala. Deliver the afternoon of the eighth day, third bell, to the SERVICE LANDING (east water-stairs). Present this order to the landing warden for admittance of the cart and one (1) porter. Signed, E. Marrow, Steward of the Household.'
inventory.name: Wine delivery order
inventory.source: stolen: coat pocket in Pell's cabinet 8, Rosewater Baths

inventory.description: Six close-written pages torn from the back of a spellbook, in a small, furious hand with diagrams. THE BLINK: at the Grand Conjunction the Orrery's last ring locks at the stroke of midnight, and the whole ward lattice goes dead for about three minutes and ten seconds. Every sigil plate, every alarm chime, and the Curator's own plate at the Undercroft door all go dark. The Brass Wardens are bound to the lattice and SHOULD stand still for the Blink ('should' underlined twice). THE HEART: a brass focal chamber in the Orrery works, directly under the great lens. Reach it by the Staff Only stair from the Rotunda, or from the Undercroft side. One door, as of eight years ago. The Eye sits in a cradle; the Orrery opens a clockwork iris over it at midnight on its own ('the lids'). THE EYE: while the lids are open it can be struck: bludgeoning or piercing only, and it's small, hard and glassy, perhaps as hard to hit as a knight in plate. Anyone in the Heart without a smoked-glass visor when the iris opens will begin to turn to stone. A Warden's gala visor will do. At the foot, underlined: 'This is how it was EIGHT YEARS AGO. She has had eight years to change it. Look before you leap. T.F.'
inventory.name: Tobias's Notes on the Blink and the Heart
inventory.source: gift: written by Tobias Fenwick in exchange for the Codex

inventory.description: A single sheet, soft at the folds, in a quick slanting hand. Dated six years ago, five days before Emeric died. 'Wyn, love, they're running tests in the Hall of Heroes at night with the lamps out. Twice now I've seen a green light under the Rotunda doors, and the next week there's a new statue in the Hall and a name gone off the duty roll. Captain Thorne asked me to look away. He says it's the Curator's business and none of ours. I won't. If anything happens to me, it wasn't thieves and it wasn't an accident, whatever they tell you. Burn this. I know you won't. E.'
inventory.name: Emeric Dane's Last Letter
inventory.source: gift: lent by Wynn Dane to 'the chapel' for the Saint's Book of Remembrance; she wants it back

inventory.description: A single sheet, soft at the folds, in a quick slanting hand. Dated six years ago, five days before Emeric died. 'Wyn, love, they're running tests in the Hall of Heroes at night with the lamps out. Twice now I've seen a green light under the Rotunda doors, and the next week there's a new statue in the Hall and a name gone off the duty roll. Captain Thorne asked me to look away. He says it's the Curator's business and none of ours. I won't. If anything happens to me, it wasn't thieves and it wasn't an accident, whatever they tell you. Burn this. I know you won't. E.'

inventory.source: gift: lent by Wynn Dane to 'the chapel' for the Saint's Book of Remembrance; she wants it back

inventory.description: Six close-written pages torn from the back of a spellbook, in a small, furious hand with diagrams. THE BLINK: at the Grand Conjunction the Orrery's last ring locks at the stroke of midnight, and the whole ward lattice goes dead for about three minutes and ten seconds. Every sigil plate, every alarm chime, and the Curator's own plate at the Undercroft door all go dark. The Brass Wardens are bound to the lattice and SHOULD stand still for the Blink ('should' underlined twice). THE HEART: a brass focal chamber in the Orrery works, directly under the great lens. Reach it by the Staff Only stair from the Rotunda, or from the Undercroft side. One door, as of eight years ago. The Eye sits in a cradle; the Orrery opens a clockwork iris over it at midnight on its own ('the lids'). THE EYE: while the lids are open it can be struck: bludgeoning or piercing only, and it's small, hard and glassy, perhaps as hard to hit as a knight in plate. Anyone in the Heart without a smoked-glass visor when the iris opens will begin to turn to stone. A Warden's gala visor will do. At the foot, underlined: 'This is how it was EIGHT YEARS AGO. She has had eight years to change it. Look before you leap. T.F.'
inventory.name: Tobias's Notes on the Blink and the Heart
inventory.source: gift: written by Tobias Fenwick in exchange for the Codex

inventory.name: Clothes, Traveler's
inventory.note: Second-hand from Nance Pettle's rag stall: a long brown wool coat gone shiny at the elbows, a grey waistcoat, a flat cloth cap. A clerk's clothes, not a magister's.

inventory.description: Her ladyship's 'terms' for a private masque, signed at the foot in Silas Whitlow's own hand: 'Accepted, on behalf of the Alcazar Players, S. A. Whitlow, Manager', with a looping W and a dash beneath. A clean sample of his signature and hand.
inventory.name: Whitlow's signed acceptance

inventory.description: A single sheet, soft at the folds, in a quick slanting hand. Dated six years ago, five days before Emeric died. 'Wyn, love, they're running tests in the Hall of Heroes at night with the lamps out. Twice now I've seen a green light under the Rotunda doors, and the next week there's a new statue in the Hall and a name gone off the duty roll. Captain Thorne asked me to look away. He says it's the Curator's business and none of ours. I won't. If anything happens to me, it wasn't thieves and it wasn't an accident, whatever they tell you. Burn this. I know you won't. E.'
inventory.name: Emeric Dane's Last Letter
inventory.source: gift: lent by Wynn Dane to 'the chapel' for the Saint's Book of Remembrance; she wants it back

inventory.description: A folded order on the Meridian's cream letter-paper, sealed with the museum's orrery stamp: 'Pellow & Sons, Vintner's Row. Sixty (60) bottles, Sable Vine '31, for the Lantern Gala. Deliver the afternoon of the eighth day, third bell, to the SERVICE LANDING (east water-stairs). Present this order to the landing warden for admittance of the cart and one (1) porter. Signed, E. Marrow, Steward of the Household.'
inventory.name: Wine delivery order

inventory.source: crafted: Sera's forgery (Calligrapher's Supplies 20 vs DC 15)

inventory.description: A heavy coin of dark gold stamped on both sides with a closed eye. The Emissary pays in these. Crane: 'He'll know it if he sees it.'
inventory.name: Black-Gold Coin
inventory.source: gift: Valentin Crane, from his waistcoat

inventory.description: Varga's Meridian Warden sigil: silver, stamped with the sun-and-key. Tuned to the museum's ward lattice. Passes the Bridge of Saints staff gate, the island's outer wards and the galleries after hours, but not the Orrery floor. It becomes an alarm once the Wardens strike Varga's name from their ledger.
inventory.name: Warden's Sigil Ring
inventory.source: stolen: pried off Sergeant Varga's chained hand in the Heron's brig

inventory.description: A single sheet, soft at the folds, in a quick slanting hand. Dated six years ago, five days before Emeric died. 'Wyn, love, they're running tests in the Hall of Heroes at night with the lamps out. Twice now I've seen a green light under the Rotunda doors, and the next week there's a new statue in the Hall and a name gone off the duty roll. Captain Thorne asked me to look away. He says it's the Curator's business and none of ours. I won't. If anything happens to me, it wasn't thieves and it wasn't an accident, whatever they tell you. Burn this. I know you won't. E.'
inventory.name: Emeric Dane's Last Letter
inventory.source: gift: lent by Wynn Dane to 'the chapel' for the Saint's Book of Remembrance; she wants it back

inventory.description: A folded order on the Meridian's cream letter-paper, sealed with the museum's orrery stamp: 'Pellow & Sons, Vintner's Row. Sixty (60) bottles, Sable Vine '31, for the Lantern Gala. Deliver the afternoon of the eighth day, third bell, to the SERVICE LANDING (east water-stairs). Present this order to the landing warden for admittance of the cart and one (1) porter. Signed, E. Marrow, Steward of the Household.'
inventory.name: Wine delivery order
inventory.source: stolen: coat pocket in Pell's cabinet 8, Rosewater Baths

inventory.description: Five iron and brass keys on a ring with a cork tag reading PELLOW & SONS - VINTNER'S ROW. Front door, cellar, counting-room, and two smaller cabinet keys.

inventory.source: stolen: coat pocket in Pell's cabinet 8, Rosewater Baths

inventory.description: Lettie's iron ring of six keys: front doors, staff door, linen room, stoke-hole, till, and a small brass one unmarked.

inventory.description: A single sheet, soft at the folds, in a quick slanting hand. Dated six years ago, five days before Emeric died. 'Wyn, love, they're running tests in the Hall of Heroes at night with the lamps out. Twice now I've seen a green light under the Rotunda doors, and the next week there's a new statue in the Hall and a name gone off the duty roll. Captain Thorne asked me to look away. He says it's the Curator's business and none of ours. I won't. If anything happens to me, it wasn't thieves and it wasn't an accident, whatever they tell you. Burn this. I know you won't. E.'

inventory.source: gift: lent by Wynn Dane to 'the chapel' for the Saint's Book of Remembrance; she wants it back
